title: JioHotstar Goes Global With Launch in UK, Canada and Singapore
excerpt: India's largest streaming platform launches internationally with 160,000 hours of content but without the live cricket that drives its massive domestic audience.
body:
• JioHotstar launched in the UK, Canada and Singapore on September 2, replacing the existing Hotstar service in those markets with a new app and brand.
  • The platform offers 160,000+ hours of entertainment content in 12 languages but will not include live sports like IPL, WPL or cricket at launch due to territorial licensing constraints.
  • JioHotstar averages 500 million monthly active users in India and is targeting 4 million+ people of Indian origin across the three new markets.
  • The US is not part of this rollout — Hotstar shut down its standalone US service in 2021, and JioStar has not announced plans for re-entry.

JioHotstar, India's largest video streaming platform, launched internationally in the United Kingdom, Canada and Singapore on September 2, marking the first time the unified JioHotstar brand operates outside India. The service replaces the existing Hotstar apps in all three markets, with current subscribers able to log in using their existing credentials.

The expansion is the first major global move by JioStar, the media joint venture between Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Industries and Walt Disney Co. formed through an $8.5 billion merger in 2024. In India, the merger combined Disney+ Hotstar and JioCinema into JioHotstar, which the company says averaged 500 million monthly active users during the quarter ending March 2026.

Entertainment Without the Cricket

The international launch comes with a notable omission: no live sports. In India, JioHotstar streams the Indian Premier League, the Women's Premier League, Indian national cricket matches, the English Premier League, and tournaments including Wimbledon and the US Open. None of these will be available in the three new markets at launch.

JioStar told TechCrunch the absence is due to existing content deals — streaming rights are typically negotiated by territory — but did not rule out adding sports in the future. The launch instead tests whether JioHotstar's entertainment catalogue alone can attract and retain an international audience.

The platform will offer more than 160,000 hours of content across over 12 languages, including Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, Kannada, Gujarati, Marathi and English. Live TV channels under the Star network — Star Plus, Colors, Star Vijay, Asianet, Star Jalsha and Star Pravah — will also be available.

New Originals and Interactive Features

JioStar is launching a slate of new original shows alongside the expansion, including Ali Baba Aur Chaalis Bhoot, Prince of Mollywood, Part Timers and The Court. Reality franchise Bigg Boss returns across six languages, and for the first time international viewers can cast live votes throughout each edition.

Viewers in Canada and the UK will get access to a 24/7 live feed for Bigg Boss, while Canadian subscribers can watch Bigg Boss Hindi seven days ahead of its television broadcast. India Ka Top 1 Percent, a new format hosted by Anil Kapoor testing contestants' logic and reasoning, will air in Canada and Singapore.

"Streaming has spent the last decade competing on the size of its catalogue. The bigger opportunity now is to reimagine how audiences experience entertainment."

— Amit Malhotra, Head of International Business, JioStar

Pricing and Market Strategy

JioHotstar has introduced quarterly and annual subscription plans across all three markets. In the UK, plans range from £19.99 (roughly $27) quarterly to £69.99 (around $95) annually. Canada starts at CA$19.99 (about $14) quarterly and CA$49.99 ($36) annually. Singapore pricing runs from SG$29.98 ($24) to SG$69.98 ($55).

By comparison, JioHotstar subscriptions in India start at Rs 79 (about $0.80) per month and top out at Rs 2,199 (around $23) annually — a fraction of what international subscribers will pay. Existing Hotstar subscribers in the UK can continue their current monthly plans as long as auto-renewal remains active.

India's Ministry of External Affairs data suggests the three launch markets are home to more than 4 million people of Indian origin, giving JioHotstar a built-in target audience. The broader South Asian diaspora could extend that reach further.

The US Gap

Notably absent from the rollout is the United States, home to the largest Indian diaspora. Hotstar previously operated a standalone service there before shutting it down in 2021. JioStar has said it plans to expand into additional markets over time but has not disclosed a timeline or strategy for the US.

JioHotstar is the second-largest streaming platform globally by subscribers, trailing only Netflix. Whether the entertainment-only approach can build a meaningful international business — particularly without the cricket rights that anchor its domestic dominance — will be the key test as the service expands beyond its home market.

nri_angle: JioHotstar's international launch directly targets the Indian diaspora in the UK, Canada and Singapore, giving NRI audiences access to the same entertainment platform popular in India — though without the cricket that many diaspora fans follow most closely.
